A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tabula-8B evaluation study despite the shortened title in v2. The complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 165 UniPredict datasets, trained Alpaca controls, and contamination investigations, with results in Sections 4 and appendices C–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including model comparisons, task-stratified analyses, and identified training-data matches.

M1.justification: The model training, inference, and contamination-search procedures remain unchanged. Section 3 expands the rationale for parallel fine-tuning controls and LoRA, which were already documented in v1 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 165 datasets and retain the same 20 held-out datasets for Alpaca+Q training. Closed-source models and table synthesis are newly discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: The majority-class, Base Llama, Alpaca, Alpaca+Q, and Tabula-8B comparisons retain their membership in corresponding experiments. GReaT, TapTap, and Tabby appear in discussion, not as newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix G.1.5 adds code, raw-prediction, and data-availability assessment criteria to the existing literature audit. The model experiments retain their training settings, held-out datasets, four-shot prompting, greedy decoding, and metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix G.1.5 adds a supplementary audit of reproducibility practices across the same five reviewed papers. Existing contamination investigations and model-control analyses are unchanged; the proposed perturbation, temporal-holdout, and extraction probes in G.3 are not performed tests.

E5.justification: The study's ANOVA, pairwise t-tests, and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged. The new discussion of CARTE's ten random splits and standard deviations describes prior work, not additional runs or uncertainty estimates for this study.

E6.justification: Model scores and contamination results in Tables 1–13 remain unchanged. New Table 14 reports reproducibility-audit findings, including the absence of released raw predictions. The previous Table 14, now Table 15, changes CARTE's identified-gap count from 6/6 to 5/6.

T1.justification: No mathematical definition, formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised. The new framework-extension discussion is qualitative.

C1.justification: The three central findings and headline percentages are retained. Although v1 already acknowledges case-study limitations, v2's conclusion explicitly distinguishes results established for Tabula-8B on UniPredict from a broader TLM 'structural conjecture,' qualifying the central claim's generality.

C2.justification: New appendices G.3–G.4 explain applicability boundaries and possible adaptations for closed-source TLMs and table synthesis. Section 6 adds machine unlearning as a possible causal contamination test, while Section 3 adds an argument about the implications of using LoRA instead of full fine-tuning.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-artifacts repository pointer on page 1 and restores omitted name and feature text in Appendix A.2.1's prompt example. These improve access information and documentation; the PDFs do not establish an underlying experimental change.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to QLoRA, TapTap, and Tabby, expands comparisons of prior papers' reproducibility practices, and positions the predictive evaluation framework relative to table synthesis. Consolidated duplicate references and publication-metadata updates do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, relocates and edits the disclaimer, expands the approach rationale, and connects recommendations to supporting findings. It also adds appendix subsections, an impact statement, and acknowledgments while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 expand from single-column to full-width displays and move within the main text. v2 adds the reproducibility table and relocates and renumbers the existing methodology scorecard, correcting its caption from five papers to four approaches.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency and precision through the artifact-access pointer, repaired prompt example, corrected CARTE tally, and clearer qualification of the conclusion. Larger plots and explicit links between findings and recommendations improve readability. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the new closed-source and synthesis extensions are explicitly conceptual, so the overall gain is limited.
